unmapped_findings: For the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl RAP matrix, the 6 wt.% Al variant has mechanical properties between the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C and the 8 wt.% Al variant; specifically, alloys with Al additions of 4 wt.% and 6 wt.% are only very weakly affected by the applied aging treatments in terms of their mechanical data compared with Fe-30Mn-1.2C (weakening/embrittlement) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (strengthening).

In Fig. 3 (line plots of YS, UTS, TE, hardness versus Al content), the 600 °C/1 h condition is shown as the olive curve for the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl series; no numeric values are printed on individual data points, so exact YS/UTS/TE/hardness for the 6Al 600 °C/1 h point are only available graphically.

The intermediate alloy variants with Al concentrations of 2-6 wt.% do not show equivalent mechanical properties compared to the ~8 wt.% Al variant, and a much smaller influence of aging on the tensile behavior is observed in the 2-6 wt.% Al cases.
